foods.name: Fresh fruit, washed
foods.why: Bananas, apples, berries, mango: all a straight yes. Give fruit a wash under the tap first, skin and all, even the bits you are not going to eat.

foods.name: Fruit cut at home
foods.why: You control the knife, the board and the clock, so fruit you wash and cut yourself is a green light. Keep it in the fridge and eat it the same day.

foods.name: Rockmelon
foods.why: Our two sources disagree here: Royal Women's allows it washed and cut at home, NSW Food Authority says skip it entirely because the rough rind traps bacteria. Stricter wins, so it is benched.
foods.swap: Watermelon, honeydew or mango, washed and cut at home, gives you the same sweet juicy hit.

foods.name: Canned and dried fruit
foods.why: Sealed tins and dried fruit are a yes any day. Dried apricots and prunes are quietly brilliant for iron and for keeping things moving along.

foods.name: Frozen vegetables
foods.why: Frozen veg is a yes once it is cooked. NSW Food Authority asks you not to eat it straight from the packet, so give it a proper hot cook first.

foods.name: Frozen fruit
foods.why: Frozen fruit is a yes. Imported frozen berries have been recalled before, so the extra-cautious move is to cook them first or pick Australian grown.

foods.name: Cooked vegetables
foods.why: Wash them, cook them, eat them: veg is where a lot of the good stuff lives. Roasted, steamed or stir fried, the whole lot is a green light.

foods.name: Canned vegetables
foods.why: Straight off the shelf and good to go. Once the tin is open, follow the storage note on the label and tip the leftovers into a container in the fridge.

foods.name: Salad made fresh at home
foods.why: Lettuce help: wash everything well, build it fresh and eat it soon after. The only thing to leave out is raw sprouts, which have their own card.

foods.name: Juice and smoothies made at home
foods.why: You are the juice bar now: washed whole fruit, your own clean blender, drunk straight away. That is the entire rule, and it is a yes.

foods.name: Cooked mushrooms
foods.why: Wash them, cook them hot, enjoy them. Grilled mushies on the big brekky are a green light, with one exception: enoki, which has its own card.

foods.name: Avocado
foods.why: Smashed, sliced or scooped straight out of the skin, avo is a green light. Rinse the skin before you cut it so the knife stays clean on the way in.

foods.name: Potatoes
foods.why: Spuds are a yes in every form you can cook them: mashed, roasted, baked or boiled. Give the skin a scrub first if the jacket is coming along too.

foods.name: Fresh herbs, washed
foods.why: Give them a good rinse and scatter away. Basil, coriander, parsley and mint are all a green light, straight from the bunch onto the plate.

foods.name: Enoki mushrooms
foods.why: Enoki has been behind listeria outbreaks here in Australia, so raw or barely wilted in a hot pot it is a no for now.
foods.makeItGreen: Cooked right through and piping hot, stir fried or simmered in a soup for a few minutes, enoki is fine.
foods.swap: Button or swiss brown mushrooms, cooked hot in the pan, do the same job in a stir fry.

foods.name: Store-bought pre-cut fruit
foods.why: Once fruit is cut it sits wet and cool for hours, which is listeria weather. Pre-cut melon is the riskiest of the lot.
foods.makeItGreen: Buy it whole, wash the skin and cut it yourself at home. Same fruit, no worries.
foods.swap: A whole banana, apple or mandarin off the same shelf: nature's own packaging.

foods.name: Shop fruit salad
foods.why: Pre-cut fruit plus an unknown amount of sitting time is exactly the combination listeria likes. Not this one for now.
foods.makeItGreen: Make it at home from washed whole fruit and eat it the same day.
foods.swap: Home-cut fruit salad with a spoon of yoghurt and a drizzle of honey on top.

foods.name: Salad bars and pre-packaged salads
foods.why: Someone else washed it, someone else cut it, and nobody can tell you how long it has been sitting out. A sneeze guard does not stop listeria.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for it made fresh in front of you, or build the very same salad at home.
foods.swap: A home-made garden salad, or hot cooked veg on the side instead.

foods.name: Raw sprouts
foods.why: NSW Food Authority benches every kind raw or lightly cooked, alfalfa through to mung. Seeds sprout in warm damp conditions, and bacteria love that too.
foods.makeItGreen: Cooked properly hot right through, tossed into a stir fry or a soup until they go soft, sprouts are back on.
foods.swap: Grated carrot, cucumber ribbons or shredded cabbage give you the same crunch in a sandwich.

foods.name: Cafe and juice-bar juices and smoothies
foods.why: Two problems in the one cup: fruit that was cut hours ago, and juicers and blenders that are genuinely hard to clean properly.
foods.makeItGreen: Blend it at home from washed whole fruit and drink it straight away, and it is a green light.
foods.swap: A bottled pasteurised juice from the fridge aisle, or a smoothie out of your own blender.
